correctness.rationale: On every strict sign mask A of the mean-centered vector, the Jacobian is D_A(I-1 mu^T/M), and every nonempty proper mask is attainable at x=1_A. A root-based expansion of any perturbation into constant plus descendant cut indicators is an isometric edge jump-basis for weighted tree-TV; thus every fixed mask's induced norm is its maximal normalized bridge-column variation. On a deleted edge splitting U,W with a=mu(U)/M,b=mu(W)/M, its centered cut has values -b on U and a on W; internal edges contribute at most b w(E[U])+a w(E[W]), the bridge at most w_e. Checkerboard activation on both components with both bridge incident vertices active simultaneously saturates all edges; for n>=3 at least one vertex is inactive, making that mask strictly realizable. Nearby x=1_A and y=x+eps 1_W attain equality without boundary ties. The n=2 two-mask case yields max(mu_i)/M. With unit weights internal tree-edge sums equal component size minus one, hence 2u(n-u)/n; nonstar tree has a nonpendant cut and path has a balanced cut. Independently enumerated all masks and edge-columns on sampled rational weighted trees of sizes 2..8 and matched the formula; no finite computation is used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: This theorem identifies a natural pairwise instability of weighted mean-centered ReLU under edge variation even while each single signal contracts. It gives an exact bridge-mass/weight law on every positively weighted tree, constructive equality masks and striking exact extremal consequences (path coefficient asymptotic n/2, stars optimal). The tree-cut geometry and simultaneous checkerboard saturation make it a structural nonlinear operator result, not an application of a known spectral inequality.

final_claim: For a finite tree with n>=3, positive vertex masses mu and edge weights w, the exact attained two-input weighted edge-TV norm of F(x)=max(x-mean_mu(x),0) is max_e[1+(mu(W_e)w(E[U_e])+mu(U_e)w(E[W_e]))/(M w_e)]; for n=2 the answer is max(mu_1,mu_2)/M. Unit weights give (2/n)max_e |U_e||W_e|, star-minimum and balanced-cut maximum.
limitations: Finite connected trees only; positive vertex masses and edge-TV weights.
No cyclic-graph, vector-input, or alternative centering theorem.
